text: The model's conformal prediction set includes two possible tumour categories, so the system cannot definitively separate them. This ambiguity is understandable because glioma and other tumours such as meningioma can show similar contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI, a recognised source of mis-classification for image-only classifiers [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. Moreover, an image-based output does not convey tumour grade, molecular subtype, margins or volume, all of which are essential for accurate characterisation and cannot be inferred reliably from a single slice [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. Symptoms and prognosis depend more on location, size and growth rate than on the broad tumour label alone, and management requires multidisciplinary input rather than imaging in isolation [nci-cns-pdq-hp] [ninds-brain-tumors]. It is therefore appropriate to discuss further investigations with a qualified professional, which may include a dedicated contrast-enhanced brain-tumour MRI protocol, specialist neurological or neurosurgical review, and, where tissue is obtained, histopathological and molecular characterisation in line with current WHO classification [nci-cns-pdq-hp] [who-cns5].
